:::{#exm-standardization}
#### Standardizing over disease severity

In the population of @exm-exchangeability-strata,
$\Pf{L = 0} = 600/1000 = 0.6$ and $\Pf{L = 1} = 0.4$,
and by consistency the observed stratum means are
$\E{Y \mid A = 1, L = l} = \E{Y(1) \mid L = l}$
and $\E{Y \mid A = 0, L = l} = \E{Y(0) \mid L = l}$.
By @thm-standardization:

$$
\ba
\E{Y(1)}
&= 10 \cdot 0.6 + 20 \cdot 0.4
&& \text{(standardization formula with } a = 1 \text{)} \\
&= 6 + 8
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= 14
&& \text{(add)} \\
\E{Y(0)}
&= 8 \cdot 0.6 + 18 \cdot 0.4
&& \text{(standardization formula with } a = 0 \text{)} \\
&= 4.8 + 7.2
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&= 12
&& \text{(add)} \\
\text{ATE}
&= 14 - 12
&& \text{(definition of ATE)} \\
&= 2
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

Standardization recovers the true ATE of 2,
whereas the naive contrast in @exm-rct-identification-fails gave 7.
Standardization weights both treatment groups' stratum means
by the same distribution of $L$,
the whole population's,
instead of each group's own distribution of $L$.

:::
